pois.name: Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof
pois.blurb: Frankfurt (Main) Hauptbahnhof (short Frankfurt (Main) Hbf, in English Frankfurt Central Station) is the busiest train station in the German state of Hesse and the second busiest train station in Germany behind Hamburg Hauptbahnhof.

image.attribution: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de

themeConnection.text: Opened in 1888 and remains an active intercity, regional, and commuter station.

pois.name: London Fenchurch Street station
pois.blurb: Fenchurch Street, also known as London Fenchurch Street, is a central London railway terminus in the south-eastern corner of the City of London.

themeConnection.text: Opened in 1841 and remains an active scheduled passenger railway station.

pois.name: Gare d'Austerlitz
pois.blurb: Gare d'Austerlitz (English: Austerlitz station), officially Paris Austerlitz, is one of the seven large Paris railway terminal stations.

image.attribution: Fred Romero from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0

themeConnection.text: Opened in 1840 and remains an active scheduled passenger railway station.

pois.name: York station
pois.blurb: York railway station is a principal stop on the East Coast Main Line (ECML) serving the cathedral city of York, in North Yorkshire, England.

themeConnection.text: Opened in 1877 and remains an active intercity and regional passenger station.

pois.name: Utrecht Centraal station
pois.blurb: Utrecht Centraal, officially Station Utrecht Centraal (Dutch: [staːˈɕɔn ˈytrɛxt sɛnˈtraːl]), is the transit hub that integrates three bicycle parkings, two bus stations, two tram stops and the central railway station for Utrecht, Netherlands.

themeConnection.text: Opened in 1843 and remains an active national passenger railway station.

pois.name: Edinburgh Waverley station
pois.blurb: Edinburgh Waverley station opened in 1866 and remains the principal railway station in Edinburgh, with frequent scheduled National Rail services.

pois.name: Berlin Ostbahnhof
pois.blurb: Berlin Ostbahnhof (German for Berlin East railway station) is a main line railway station in Berlin, Germany. It is located in the Friedrichshain quarter, now part of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg borough, and has undergone several name changes in its history.

pois.name: Madrid Atocha railway station

pois.name: Wien Westbahnhof

theme.title: Operating Passenger Railway Stations Opened Before 1900
theme.introduction: Before air travel, grand stations were gateways to the wider world. These historic terminals still carry passengers today.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include only a location satisfying every condition: (1) it is an individually named railway station with platforms or a station building that can be pinned as one exact map location; (2) scheduled passenger rail service began at that same identifiable site on or before 31 December 1899, even if the station building was later rebuilt or replaced; (3) the station currently has regularly scheduled passenger trains on the date of play, including intercity, regional, commuter, or national rail; (4) the station lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (5) the qualifying historical opening date and present passenger operation are documented or generally unambiguous.
